text: The left ribbon is replaced by a top tab bar: one tab per cluster with its state mark, slug and context gauge; New cluster and Discard are reachable from the bar; the cluster Edit action is dropped from the UI.

A cluster tab shows three panels side by side, filesystem, chat and terminal, split by draggable separators, with minimize and maximize controls (at most two minimized, maximize minimizes the other two), a layout persisted per cluster in the browser, and a phone layout.

The terminal panel holds several terminal tabs, each an interactive shell in the cluster workdir on a chosen agent pod, over a WebSocket PTY served by the wrapper and proxied by the orchestrator api, rendered with xterm.js.
The filesystem panel shows the cluster's shared workdir as a lazily loaded tree (VS Code explorer style), refreshed when the event stream shows a write, with a read-only file preview.
New backend surface: a wrapper file and terminal API and orchestrator /api/v1 proxies for both, with path confinement, size caps and terminal caps.
Every WebSocket upgrade is checked against a mandatory Origin allowlist (ORCH_ALLOWED_ORIGINS) beside the existing source allowlist.
Deployed: the wrapper image, the orchestrator image and chart are pinned in agents-helmfile; apply and smoke are run by the user after the epic.

Q14: this epic builds the hamburger menu at the top left: every session (cluster) listed from the top and a settings section pinned to the bottom that stays empty until the cluster-presets epic adds Presets.
Q2: the per-agent rows (pod, state, free since, own gauge) move into an agents strip in the chat panel header, merged with the agent filter chips.
